name: Delta
author: Luke "DELTA" Zelezny

provenance.from: Ultimate Amiga forum, AMOS Factory downloads section, retrieved 2026-07-26. Most items there are credited "provided and archived by Lonewolf10". Archive path: Delta.
provenance.note: Documentation coverage was measured by counting how many of the library's own keyword names appear in the files shipped beside it, taking only files that can be documentation (not disk images, example programs or the library itself). That measures the DOCUMENTATION, which is what the `docs` field records; it does not set the evidence tier, which follows from what is available to read.
provenance.redistribution: Third-party extension, redistribution terms unverified unless stated in the notes. Kept as a fixture for identification and reference only.

notes: Lukasz "DELTA" Zelezny's public-domain toolbox -- "This is small extension for AMOSPro. If you like it then send me post-card." Fourteen instructions that poke the hardware and twelve functions that return constants. Read from the 1,936-byte hunk (30 jump-table entries, 26 of them keywords) against an AmigaGuide that covers every one briefly; the slot is the guide's install note and routine 0's `moveq #$e,d0`, and there is no data zone at all. FIVE of the instructions are Misc 1.0's routines instruction for instruction -- Delta Drive Motor On/Off is Dled On/Off, Delta Mouse Off is Mouse Off, Delta Change Disk is Disk Wait, Delta Wait Fire is Firewait -- and Delta Reset is Misc's Reset, so the half of this extension that touches the machine arrives with a witness whose own assembler source is published, including Misc's inverted drive-motor defect, which Delta inherits whole. Its own defects: every one of the nine string functions uses `movea.w (buffer).L` where `lea` was wanted, so it reads the WORD AT its twenty-byte buffer, gets zero, and builds the string AT ADDRESS ZERO -- it works, because the pointer handed back is read the same wrong way and is zero too, and the price is the 68000's exception vectors (Delta About$ writes 24 bytes, vectors 0 to 5). `Delta Inter On` writes $0000 to INTENA, whose bit 15 chooses set or clear, so it clears nothing and does nothing, while `Delta Inter Off` really does take INTEN down -- interrupts can be turned off and not back on. `Delta Decrunch XX` is a LONGWORD write to COLOR00, so the value lands in COLOR01 and colour 0 goes black, the reverse of the guide; its range checks are word tests and `cmpi.w #$1000` is signed, so negatives pass and 65536 is refused. `Delta Wait Double Mouse` never waits for a release between its two presses. `Delta Pal` writes BEAMCON0's HIGH half by byte and only reaches the PAL bit because the 68000 duplicates a byte across the data bus. The table listed this row as needing intuition.library, grouped with Delta 1.6; 1.4 needs nothing -- the only "intuition.library" string in the binary sits in a routine past the last keyword that nothing calls.
